how_to_steps.text: Select the document suitable for your needs.
Add details or facts to the document but do not sign the form.
Take your document to an authorised witness (you may need to book an appointment first).
Prove your identity to the witness (if you have known them for less than 12 months).
Sign the document in the presence of the authorised witness.

faqs.a: A statutory declaration is a written statement that a person swears, affirms, or declares to be true in the presence of an authorised witness.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to prove my identity?
faqs.a: You need proof of identity documents, such as a driver licence or permit with your photo, NSW Photo Card, Australian proof of age card, Australian passport, or a passport/similar document from a country other than Australia or the UN.

faqs.q: Do I need to book an appointment with the witness?
faqs.a: It is recommended to ask if your identification document is acceptable when you book an appointment with the authorised witness.
